cause: The page's position on the bridge was only ever in the narration (crossing, still crossing, far side, getting smaller) and never in the notebook, so the DM put him back mid-bridge for the new scene without tracking where he had got to.

In one paragraph the DM wrote that Tobin rides on to Thornhallow tonight and that he lodges at the inn and leaves at dawn; the notebook note written the same round also holds both 'sending him on tonight' and 'lodging at the Drowned Candle'.

The notebook said Garrow followed Wren out of Marrowford and Thornhallow is downriver, but Tobin had just said the man came to the kitchens yesterday, and the DM wrote 'upriver ... the same day' without checking either.
The DM had just listed a cook, a pot-boy and a kitchen-maid (and its note says three heard), then wrote 'twelve pairs of eyes' as a loose figure without counting the room.

Edric only 'half-suspected' the Aldermere marriage, but the DM then gave him a vivid memory of his grandmother Maud Fenn as a made-up flourish; it clashes mildly, though a lord could know her name and still believe the family story.
The wagon left at dawn and it is half past one, about seven hours, but the DM wrote 'an hour or two of start' in the same reply as the fishwife's 'gone at dawn' without working out the difference.

In R28 Marta said Corvin gave the lamp over her door, and that line never went into the notebook; in R30 the DM invented a new story of Corvin sitting up all night over the lamp on his first stay, which clashes.

Narration (and Corvin's note) said short sword, but the fight tool's generic bandit stat block rolled a scimitar; the DM kept the earlier narration and the tool label disagrees, so the clash is between game output and story.
The tool line showed d20 [3] + 3 = 6, but the DM reported the bare die (3) as the check result and forgot to add the modifier.
Kit had only been named as a man-at-arms with no stated sex, so the DM wrote 'he' here and only fixed her as a woman when it created her entry one round later.
The broken hairpin jamming the lock was only in R2 narration, never in the notebook, and 43 rounds later the DM opened the box with the key without remembering the jam.
The notebook said Lady Maren gave Wren a guest room, but the DM reused the Thornhallow 'small room under the eaves' phrase from R25 and moved it to Ashby Weir.

Kit was only shown with a spear, never given a shield or sword in the notes; when the party tool built her as a fighter it used the default fighter kit and the DM copied that into the notebook and narration.
In the same reply the arbiter says she will hear Wren 'this afternoon' while the DM's closing narration says the account is owed at noon, and the hearing time was only fixed in the next round.

The notebook said Elowen passed through about twenty years ago and the keeper held the staff twenty years, so 'twenty years' fit then; the clash comes from the later invention that Elowen died sixteen years ago and that Corvin was turned away at the Wick-House.
The unnamed watcher's passive Perception was set at 12 on the spot and the number was not written down; when the same figure turned out to be Sparrow the DM used 13.
The oil was thrown two rounds earlier and removed from the sheet, but inventory lives on the sheet and not the notebook, and the DM suggested hurling it again without checking.
The notebook said the light had been dark fifteen years since the channel moved, and the DM then invented that Brann kept it dark by Elowen's word; the entry was not in the shown notes.
Brann forecast a squall 'by afternoon, hours yet' and the DM then dropped it on the skiff at 8:20 AM, ignoring the forecast the notebook held.

Corvin's cache note said 'H. watches the east door' and the notebook also had Hale held at Thornhallow, but the DM in R97 settled H. as Master Hale without checking the note, which was not in the shown notes.
Wren's age of nineteen (opening, and R70) was in neither the summary nor the notebook, so the DM invented that Corvin took her at four or five, which makes about fifteen years rather than nineteen.
Brann said Elowen reached the spit fevered in autumn and died that winter, and the DM then invented a midwinter return to Rushlight House; the timeline is strained but not strictly impossible.
The notebook said the watcher sat a quarter mile off and his horse waited beyond the crest, and the DM then wrote 'a dark mile away' loosely without recalling the figure.
The DM ruled the assize on the 30th and 'twenty days' away at R102 but only 'month's end' went into the notebook, so 'twenty days' came back as 'the twentieth' at R116.
